extracted.intended_audience: aspiring novelists and fiction writers (authors, agents, and editors interested in craft for commercial/breakout novels)
extracted.subtask_description: Crafting a 'breakout' commercial novel by engineering tension, layered plotting, strong characters, and scene-level craft so the work rises beyond solid genre fiction into memorable, emotionally resonant fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tension on Every Page
rubrics_metrics.description: "Tension on every page is the secret of great storytelling." Even quiet scenes need micro-tension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make every page deliver some form of tension — emotional, informational, anticipatory — so reader engagement never lapses. Treat this as a unifying principle that applies at scene and line level; quiet scenes still require subtle strains that move the story forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters must be three-dimensional and contradictory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build characters with complexity and internal contradictions so they feel alive and unpredictable; avoid flat or purely functional characters. Three-dimensionality supports surprising choices and deeper emotional payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inner conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters should be at war with themselves, not just facing outside obstacles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize psychological and moral tensions within characters (beliefs, desires, fears) that complicate their external decisions. Inner conflict amplifies drama and makes outcomes emotionally meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal stakes
rubrics_metrics.description: The protagonist must risk something they care about (not just 'save the world').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure stakes are personal and urgent to the protagonist — testable by the High Stakes Test (see separate metric). External or plot-scale stakes are weaker unless they tie to the character's personal values and losses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot layers
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple storylines that interweave and amplify the main narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use parallel plots, subplots, and thematic echoes to create depth and momentum; layers should interact to raise stakes, complicate choices, and enrich theme rather than merely add events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powerful scenes (every scene must turn a value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every scene must 'turn a value' — i.e., change something consequential in status, knowledge, desire, or stakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid filler scenes. Each scene should alter the story's values (relationships, information, power, emotional states). 'Turning a value' makes scenes consequential and propels narrative change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro-tension
rubrics_metrics.description: Line-by-line tension within and between scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft sentences and beats so tension accumulates within a scene and leads into the next. Use sentence-level choices (wording, withheld detail, pacing) and scene transitions to sustain reader investment continuously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tension sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Catalog of means to generate tension: conflict (external), inner conflict, bridging conflict, anticipation, dread, curiosity, withheld information, time pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ these devices deliberately and in combination. Examples: withhold critical information to generate curiosity; use time pressure to raise urgency; insert 'bridging conflicts' between major beats to maintain forward motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: High Stakes Test
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the protagonist could lose something irreplaceable; whether goals/dreams/life are genuinely at risk; whether emotional, physical, and spiritual stakes are engaged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this checklist as a litmus test for whether stakes feel real and consequential. If the answers are weak, deepen the protagonist's personal exposure or reframe threats so loss would be devastating on multiple levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing Principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Vary pace deliberately — alternate high-tension scenes with reflective ones; pure intensity exhausts and pure reflection bores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design an intentional rhythm: use high-tension sequences to drive propulsion and reflective/quiet scenes to deepen character and theme. Avoid unrelenting intensity and long stretches of low engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breakout vs. Solid (criteria for a breakout novel)
rubrics_metrics.description: A solid novel is competent genre work; a breakout novel breaks beyond convention through unique voice, larger-than-genre themes, surprising character depth, unforgettable scenes, and resonant emotional truth. Maass argues breakouts are engineered through deliberate craft choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim beyond genre competence: cultivate a distinct narrative voice, broaden themes to have universal resonance, deepen characters to surprise readers, and compose scenes that linger. Treat breakout qualities as goals achievable through specific scene- and character-level techniques rather than as accidental.
